The most powerful refutation among the options is that it is impossible to calculate all the consequences of one's acts. Bentham's felicific calculus requires summing the pleasures and pains of every consequence, including far-reaching and unforeseeable ones, so if those effects cannot be known and totalled the calculus cannot be used. That pain and pleasure are inevitable features of life does not refute it, because the calculus is built to weigh exactly those features.

CONFIDENCE: 88
